# Archived Q out-umbrella inputs

Read-only repository: https://github.com/michellab/CypAcatalysis_input
Commit: 7310aa36088e140f8197b626cd2998c740016eb3
Local clone: q-inputs-recovery. No imported code or simulation was executed.

out_plumed_inventory.json stores decompressed PLUMED input text with original paths. out_plumed_summary.json records the complete window count: 24 WT windows, 23 mutant windows for each variant. Every mutant window and 23 WT windows have an F113 torsion restraint and a distance upper wall. WT plumed_0.dat.gz is the exception.

Representative WT source: https://github.com/michellab/CypAcatalysis_input/blob/7310aa36088e140f8197b626cd2998c740016eb3/umbrella_sampling/Enzyme_F113out/WT%2BAAPF/US_omega/plumed_input/plumed_-0_25.dat.gz

Line references apply to decompressed text. Lines 3-7 define the combined centre of mass of the F60/F113 phenyl-ring atoms and its distance to the proline-ring centre of mass. Lines 11-13 apply the omega umbrella, the F113 torsion restraint and the distance upper wall. The WT torsion coefficient is 200, target -1 rad. Mutants use 300 at the same target. All inspected distance walls use coefficient 300 and threshold 0.4; there are no UNITS overrides.

Official PLUMED v2.3 manual https://www.plumed.org/doc-v2.3/user-doc/manual.pdf section 4.1 (PDF pp.55-56) gives default kJ/mol and nm units. Section 7.11 gives the upper-wall expression and defaults. With those conventions the distance bias is

\[
V(d)=\begin{cases}
300\left(\dfrac{d-0.4\,\mathrm{nm}}{1\,\mathrm{nm}}\right)^2\,\mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}, & d>0.4\,\mathrm{nm},\\
0, & d\leq0.4\,\mathrm{nm}.
\end{cases}
\]

The numeric wall coefficient is an energy constant with the default length rescaling in that expression. It is not a harmonic torsion coefficient and there is no one-half factor in this wall definition. The paper's radian units attached to distance are dimensionally inconsistent.

All inspected apo topology headers name charmm22star.ff. Seven in/out umbrella topology headers name amber99sb_modified.ff; WT out omega has no topology in its omega directory, though preparatory directories contain topologies. No actual forcefield directories are supplied in this clone, so include names do not recover the numerical modified forcefield.

These findings concern archived inputs. They do not map each window to the six published repeats or establish which auxiliary biases were removed in analysis. The exceptional WT zero window, missing mutant zero windows, actual build/version and input-to-profile mapping remain unresolved. Defining the physical reference ensemble requires that provenance before an electronic correction can be attached to Q's profiles.
contexts.where: The reported audit of the frozen input archive found omega-only biases in enzyme in inputs, whereas most out inputs additionally restrain Phe113 and apply a pooled-ring distance wall.

contexts.quote:
## Source audit

The repository is frozen at commit
`7310aa36088e140f8197b626cd2998c740016eb3`.
`in_plumed_inventory.json` records decompressed source lines and compressed-file
SHA256 values for every archived in umbrella input. Counts in `US/plumed_input`
are WT 24, ST 23, STCS 23 and STCSIV 23. STCS additionally has 23 files directly
under `US`, giving 46 archived files with 23 window names. These copies are not
evidence for 46 independent windows or repeats.

Every enzyme in input biases only omega. None defines or prints Phe113 chi1,
and none adds a chi1 restraint or centre-of-mass wall. WT/ST print omega,
omega2 (the same atom quadruplet), the omega bias and four hydrogen-bond
distances. STCS/STCSIV print omega, omega2 and the omega bias only.
Representative `plumed_1_5.dat.gz` declarations occur at decompressed lines
12-14 for WT/ST and 8-9 for STCS/STCSIV.

`Enzyme_F113in/AAPF` has 22 PLUMED files byte-identical to the corresponding
solvent AAPF files. It represents the free-substrate control. No archived
COLVAR, COLDIST, HILLS, XTC, TRR or XVG file was found. Coordinates and
checkpoints cannot supply rotamer occupancy throughout the umbrella windows.

The out audit in ledger entries 37, 38, 40 and 44 established additional chi1
and combined-ring COM biases for most windows, with the WT zero exception.
Thus the archive establishes different input bias conventions, while mapping
these files to the published profiles remains unresolved.
